thread:
emma: Heads up — production p99 for model-redwood-alpha just jumped from ~850ms to ~2.6s starting ~08:10 UTC. Customers reporting slow chat and some timeouts. escalating to support.
mike: noted. any recent deploys or config changes? :eyes:
emma: We onboarded alpha-v2 this morning (BPE merge enabled by default). Canary looked fine on small seq lengths but we have bigger traffic now.
oliver: I saw the alert from alerts-bot about long-context request latency. Link: https://dash.redwood/local/alerts/ALRT-4278
alerts-bot: alert triggered: model-redwood-alpha p99 latency > 2s for > 5m; affected hosts: gpu-nj-04,gpu-nj-07
maya: tagging eng-oncall — @mike @oliver can you take a look at kv-cache hit rates? might be eviction regressions with the new tokenizer merging prefixes.
mike: jumping in. pulling traces now. can everyone paste a sample trace id if you have one?
emma: trace id from customer ticket #CS-1138: trace_2026_08_10_9312
oliver: looking — the trace shows repeated cache misses on prefix keys, lots of re-encoding in tokenization stage. suspect BPE merge created longer token sequences earlier in pipeline causing more KV churn.
mike: running a quick repro against canary with long prompt: `curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/gen -d '{"model":"model-redwood-alpha","input": "<5000 char doc>"}'` — local p95 ~1.1s, p99 ~1.9s on canary. On prod it's 2.6s.
maya: can you capture profiler on one host? `ssh gpu-nj-07 sudo /usr/local/bin/profiler --pid $(pgrep redwood-runner) --duration 30s` — especially tokenization time and kv-store ops.
mike: ran profiler; tokenization time per request increased by ~30% and kv-store ops per token increased ~2.7x. attaching snippet:
```
TOKENIZE:  120ms -> 160ms
KV_LOOKUPS:  4.2k -> 11.3k
KV_LOOKUP_LATENCY_P50: 0.6ms -> 0.9ms
KV_EVICTIONS:  spikes concurrent with long-context sessions
```
emma: so BPE merge reduces token count for some inputs but increases variability causing different prefix alignments -> cache fragmentation. That explains the higher KV ops.
oliver: also noticed that the new model variant's chunking broke our prefix caching heuristic (we key by tokenized prefix bytes). The merge changes bytes offsets which invalidates many existing cache entries.
mike: mitigation options:
  1) Roll back to alpha-v1 (safe, immediate) — degrade new model perf for those who wanted it.
  2) Toggle off BPE merge at tokenization stage for prod (flag) — local fix but model mismatch.
  3) Warmup KV cache by replaying recent prefixes (complex, risky).
  4) Route long-context (>2048 tokens) traffic to dedicated pool with larger KV config (temporary).
emma: customer SLA impact is material. I'd prefer option 1 or 2 for short-term.
cs-oncall: customer-facing: I'll inform impacted customers we're rolling back a model variant and expect latency improvement in ~15-30m. Draft reply: "We're rolling back a model variant that caused increased latency for long conversations. You may see improved p95/p99 once the rollback finishes; we're monitoring." ok?
maya: agree. rolling back shows ~immediately for new requests but existing cached sessions might still be hit.
mike: executing rollback now: `deploy-bot rollback --service=model-redwood-alpha --to=alpha-v1 --reason="kvcache fragmentation after bpe-merge"`
deploy-bot: rollout started: rollback to alpha-v1 initiated by mike; estimated completion 9m
emma: monitoring dashboards. p95 dropped to 1.0s at 08:28 UTC, p99 down to 1.4s. still some tail but trending.
oliver: can we add a short-term routing rule: if seq_len > 2048, prefer nodes with kv-config large-cache=true? safer than forcing everyone back.
mike: good idea — adding route policy: `rbac route add --model model-redwood-alpha --expr "seq_len>2048" --target pool=large-kv --priority=50`
maya: applied. verifying metrics for large-kv pool — CPU/GPU looks fine.
emma: cs-oncall: update to customers: rolled back model variant + applied routing rule for long contexts; asking them to re-test and send traces if they still see tail latency.
cs-oncall: will update. also opening internal postmortem ticket: PM-1482.
oliver: root-cause notes to capture: tokenization BPE merge changed prefix byte alignment and invalidated prefix-key strategy; coupled with KV cache eviction settings and long-session churn -> p99 spike.
mike: next steps (action items):
  - eng-ml: evaluate tokenization-stable keying (hash of normalized tokens) to avoid byte-offset fragility — owner: oliver — ETA 2 weeks
  - eng-runtime: add KV cache warmup tooling + metrics for prefix hit rate by model variant — owner: maya — ETA 1 week
  - devex: add canary tests for long-context regen with BPE variations — owner: emma — ETA 3 days
  - ops: keep routing rule until hotfix deployed; revert when safe — owner: mike — ETA until postmortem done
emma: also propose feature flag default OFF for experimental tokenization merges during onboarding, require perf signoff before enabling in prod.
oliver: logging item — add tokenization-variant metadata to traces to quickly correlate spikes.
mike: closing notes: rollback + routing restored baseline; leaving ticket open for follow-ups. thanks all :thumbsup:
cs-oncall: customer update posted in CS-1138. will follow up if they confirm fix.
alerts-bot: alert resolved: model-redwood-alpha p99 latency back within threshold.
emma: marking thread resolved but keeping links in PM-1482. good catch team."
